clauses.anchor: Report 1 s1-4: only timers present at an update's start run; removed work does not run later in that update; new work waits for a later update and its own delay

clauses.anchor: Report 2 s1: a throwing callback is invoked once, retired and reported without stopping unrelated callbacks or clock updates
Report 2 s3: completing, removing, failing or round-ending a named timer removes its `TimersID` mapping
Report 2 s4: round end preserves KEEPALIVE timers and their usable names; removing a retired timer stays harmless
Report 3 s1-2: countdown/duration bookkeeping belongs to each timer; a shared options table is not consumed or modified
Report 3 s3-4: COUNTDOWN reports its remaining count through `TimerCount`; DURATION runs floor(duration/delay) times, zero for a shorter duration
Report 3 s5-6: invalid counts, negative durations, nonnumeric delay/duration, nonfunction callbacks or incompatible flags return -1; an invalid AddTimerByName replacement keeps the previous timer
Report 3 s7: callback parameter tables keep their shared identity
Report 3 s8-9: preserve opaque non-null payloads (integers, arrays) for ordinary and DURATION_VARIANT callbacks; do not wrap, clone or reject them
Report 3 s10: COUNTDOWN and DURATION reject non-table payloads atomically with -1
Report 3 s11: "Existing MoreSI team-change refresh and delayed LinGe event delivery must still work."
Report 3: "Keep the minimum delay of 0.1 seconds."

Report 4 s4: countdowns that disallow negatives clamp at zero across a long update; allowing negatives crosses zero
Report 4 s5: ReadTimer reports the value at read time
Report 4 s6: independent named clocks; null for an unknown name

known_issues: benchmarks/l4d2-core/private/harbor/l4d2-vslib-scheduler-persistence-hard/tests/verify.py:parse_results: the suite is one server boot. A missing or non-unique FINAL marker, or conflicting duplicate case markers, raises SubmissionFailure before any case line is printed, so every case is unobserved and the evaluator reports an incomplete (not a failing) result.

benchmarks/l4d2-core/private/harbor/l4d2-vslib-scheduler-persistence-hard/tests/suite.nut: the clock cases compare engine Time() readings with a 0.006 s tolerance inside one tick; they are deterministic in engine time but depend on the scheduler being driven by the trusted Tick driver.

The alternative control is reference-derived (reversed due-timer order, exponent float encoding, space-separated arrays); it is evidence that the suite does not pin those representation choices, not an independent implementation.
